newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-BECKER BACK WITH WIN, STICH OUT OF GERMAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BECKER BACK WITH WIN, STICH OUT OF GERMAN OPEN.

text.p: Boris Becker won his first ATP match for nearly three months on Wednesday but compatriot Michael Stich disappointingly fell at the first hurdle in his last appearance at the German Open.

Former world number one Becker has been suffering with a long-term wrist injury but came through without incident to beat 19-year-old fellow German Nicolas Kiefer 7-5 6-2 in the second round of the clay-court tournament.
Stich, who recently announced he will retire in September, faded against Czech Slava Dozedel and lost 7-6 6-2 in windy conditions.
Becker faced an awkward task against a player he has been coaching for six months in his role as head of the national training squad but said he treated it as "just another match".
"It could have been a difficult match for both players but I think we did it right and avoided any funny moments," he said.
He had a scare while serving for the match as he fell and landed with much of his weight on his troublesome wrist but suffered no damage, saying: "I'm okay but I didn't feel good for a few moments."
Becker, who surprisingly lost to Italian Renzo Furlan in the first round at Monte Carlo two weeks ago, produced a reasonably consistent performance in difficult conditions.
He had some alarms in the sixth game of the opening set when he dropped serve but he broke back immediately.
He broke again at 5-5 after Kiefer had tried an ambitious serve and volley at 30-40 and found himself stranded by Becker's pass.
After Becker had served out to love to take the first set he looked much more in control, breaking Kiefer three times with just one break back.
"Obviously this surface, clay, is the hardest on which to come back but I have to come back some time," Becker said.

"I will feel better and fitter if I can win a couple of matches. When you have such a serious injury and in such an important spot for a tennis player there are always days when you still feel it, especially when it is cold."
Former Wimbledon champion and 16th seed Stich looked increasingly inhibited by his perennial shoulder problems after missing chances in the first set tie-break.
However, there was good news for the home fans as another German caused the surprise of the day.
Tommy Haas, ranked 114 places below the ninth-rated Spaniard Carlos Moya, beat the Australian Open finalist 6-4 6-1.
Moya, seeded four, looked dispirited by the cold, windy conditions and when he came back 2-5 to 4-5 in the first set he had his momentum broken by a shower which stopped play for 20 minutes.
On resumption, Moya immediately dropped serve, sank deeper into his gloom, dropped again, and never recovered his will to fight. In frustration he blasted the last ball metres over the baseline.
However, another Spaniard, Felix Mantilla, took advantage of the interruptions to recover from difficulties to beat Sweden's Magnus Larsson 6-7 6-4 6-3.
After losing the opening tie-break Mantilla kept pounding away with his heavily topspun ground strokes even when the hailstones were pelting down at 4-4 in the second set.

He broke Larsson's serve and gave himself a psychological boost just before everyone ran for cover. When he returned, Mantilla served out to love for the second set, broke at the first attempt in the third and carried on solidly for victory.
Later Mantilla won again, thrashing compatriot Roberto Carretero 6-1 6-1 as the tournament sought to make up for time lost to the weather. His reward is a meeting on Thursday with Becker.
